title: Draw mapped shape and linetype; scale_shape / scale_linetype
description:
The discrete scales already train 'shape' and 'linetype' (CATEGORICAL_AESTHETICS, palettes.SHAPES / LINETYPES) but the geoms ignore them.
- geoms/point.py: draw each row's shape: circle (Dot), triangle, square, cross, diamond, star, plus (manim Dot/Triangle/Square/Cross/RegularPolygon/Star) normalised to equal visual area for a given 'size'; filled vs hollow variants (shape='circle_open' etc.) using stroke in 'color' and fill in 'fill'/'color'; vectorise by grouping rows per shape. Constant shape= param accepted.
- geoms/line.py (+ smooth fit line, function, vline/hline): apply linetype via DashedVMobject with dash patterns: solid, dashed, dotted, dashdot, longdash, twodash (dash_length/dashed_ratio in scene units, so appearance is independent of path length); constant linetype= param.
- geoms/base.py draw_key: keys reflect shape and linetype so legends are correct; KEY_SIZE normalisation.
- scale_shape(solid=True), scale_shape_manual(values), scale_linetype(), scale_linetype_manual(values) registered + exported; defaults already come from default_scale_for.
- Tests: point layer with 3 shapes produces the 3 mobject types; dashed line has >1 submobject; manual shape names validated with a helpful error listing SHAPES; legend glyphs match mapping.
acceptance_criteria: aes(shape='g') and aes(linetype='g') visibly differ per level in a render and in structural tests; legends show the right glyphs; constant shape/linetype params work.

title: Continuous colour/fill scales and colourbar guide
description:
scales/colour.py (new): ScaleContinuousColour(ScaleContinuous) mapping transformed values in [lo, hi] to colours by interpolating a gradient in a perceptual space (Oklab or CIE-LCh; implement the few conversion formulas in palettes.py next to hcl_to_hex, no new deps). na_value grey50 (NA_COLOR).
- Constructors (color + fill, with 'colour' aliases via the existing alias helper): scale_color_gradient(low, high), scale_color_gradient2(low, mid, high, midpoint), scale_color_gradientn(colours, values), scale_color_viridis_c(option='viridis'|'magma'|'plasma'|'inferno'|'cividis', begin, end, direction), scale_color_distiller later. Vendor the viridis family tables (CC0, from matplotlib's _cm_listed) in palettes.py as 256-entry hex lists; also add scale_color_viridis_d / scale_fill_viridis_d (discrete sampling of the same tables) and scale_color_hue(h, c, l) built on hue_pal.
- scales/discrete.default_scale_for: numeric colour/fill columns -> ScaleContinuousColour (viridis by default? ggplot uses gradient '#132B43'->'#56B1F7'; use ggplot's default for parity) instead of NotImplementedError; booleans stay discrete. build.map_non_position must train continuous and discrete non-position scales alike (today it iterates CATEGORICAL_AESTHETICS only).
- guides.py: Colourbar(VGroup) guide: a vertical bar made of N thin filled Rectangles (robust across renderers; avoid sheen gradients) with tick marks + labels at scale.get_breaks(), title from labels; horizontal variant when legend_position is top/bottom; place_legends handles Legend and Colourbar uniformly; guide_colorbar(barwidth, barheight, nbin, reverse, title) and guide='colourbar'|'legend' on the scale (legend = binned keys).
- Tests: interpolation endpoints and midpoint; limits/oob on colour; default scale selection by dtype; colourbar label count == breaks; colour+fill numeric on the same column -> one colourbar.
acceptance_criteria: aes(color='numeric_col') builds and shows a colourbar; viridis options render distinct palettes; unit tests without manim for the colour scale; structural tests for the colourbar glyphs.

title: Discrete position scales (scale_x_discrete / scale_y_discrete)
description:
Add ScaleDiscretePosition in scales/discrete.py exposing the same position-scale API that build.py and coords.py use for ScaleContinuousPosition (train / train_transformed / transform / map / map_transformed / get_limits / get_expanded_limits / dimension / get_breaks(limits) / get_labels(limits)); see the API table at the top of scales/continuous.py.
- Levels -> integer positions 1..n (pandas Categorical order, else first-seen or sorted per ggplot's rules); limits= reorders/subsets levels; breaks/labels overrides; drop unused levels option; expansion default add=0.6 (ggplot discrete default); continuous values mapped onto a discrete scale pass through (ggplot allows numeric x on a discrete axis, e.g. x=1.5 between levels).
- build.py: remove the BuildError seams in _position_scale/_check_numeric; pick the default position scale by dtype (is_discrete from stats.base); keep user scale override; the 'x'/'y' transformed columns become floats so every geom works unchanged.
- coords.py: ticks at integer positions with level labels; no grid minor lines between levels; axis title default = column name.
- geoms/col.py: default bar width 0.9 of the level spacing on a discrete axis (resolution-based on continuous as today).
- scale_x_discrete / scale_y_discrete(name, limits, breaks, labels, expand) registered + exported; aliases via aesthetics=.
- Tests: bar chart with string x; points with Categorical x in explicit order; limits= subsetting drops rows (censor) and warns; labels override; expansion; mixed layers sharing the scale accumulate levels in encounter order.
acceptance_criteria: ggplot(df, aes('category', 'value')).geom_col().build() works with string x; level order follows Categorical; tick labels are the level names; unit tests for the scale class without manim; existing tests unchanged.

title: Phase 2 — scales & guides
description: Complete the scale/guide layer of the grammar on top of the Phase 1 pipeline (build.py steps 3-4, 6-7, 9). Goals: discrete position scales; continuous colour/size/alpha scales with colourbar and binned legends; shape and linetype actually drawn; guide_legend/guide_colorbar options and legend placement; tick-label formatters and break helpers; coord zoom vs scale-limit semantics with geometric clipping; date scales; richer theme elements. See PLAN.md §3 Phase 2. Phase 1 left explicit NotImplemented/BuildError seams for most of these: build._position_scale/_check_numeric (discrete x/y), scales.discrete.default_scale_for (numeric colour), build.apply_positions (positions — Phase 3), geoms/point.py ignores 'shape', geoms/line.py ignores 'linetype'.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads closed; pytest/ruff/mypy green in CI; examples/gallery renders a categorical bar chart, a colourbar plot, a shape+linetype legend plot and a size legend plot; README documents the new scales.

title: Continuous size / alpha / linewidth scales with binned legends
description:
Today mapped numeric size/alpha pass through unscaled (point.py uses 'size' as the dot radius in scene units; line.py uses 'alpha' raw), producing huge dots / nonsense opacity.
- scales/continuous.py: ScaleContinuousRange (a ScaleContinuous whose map() rescales transformed values linearly into range=(lo, hi)); constructors scale_size(range=(0.03, 0.15)) — area-proportional by default like ggplot's scale_size_area semantics option, scale_size_area(max_size), scale_radius, scale_alpha(range=(0.1, 1)), scale_linewidth(range=(1, 6)); 'size' remains in scene units at the output so geoms are unchanged.
- discrete size/alpha: ScaleDiscrete for ordered factors mapping to evenly spaced values in range (ggplot warns for unordered factors — emit a warning).
- build.map_non_position: default scales for numeric size/alpha/linewidth columns; constants in params (geom_point(size=0.08)) bypass scales as today.
- guides.py: legend for continuous size/alpha: ~4-5 keys at scale.get_breaks() with glyphs drawn via Geom.draw_key at the mapped size/alpha; merged with a colour legend when they map the same column (same title and breaks), as ggplot does.
- Tests: map() endpoints equal range; area vs radius semantics; legend key count; default scale selection; constant size bypasses.
acceptance_criteria: aes(size='numeric_col') gives dots within range with a 4-5 key legend; aes(alpha=...) maps into (0.1, 1); unit + structural tests; the huge-dot regression is covered.

title: Build pipeline and GGPlot mobject
description:
Create build.py and mobjects.py; wire the 9 steps from PLAN.md §2 as separate functions:
1 resolve layer data/mapping (inherit_aes) and evaluate aes expressions; 2 assign PANEL (single panel in Phase 1, but keep the column so facets slot in); 3 compute stats; 4 train+map non-position scales; 5 positions (identity only in Phase 1); 6 train position scales — only on layers that actually have x/y data (intercept-only layers contribute their intercepts) — and apply user limits/transforms; 7 coord builds Axes; 8 geoms draw; 9 assemble.
- Default scales are created on demand per aesthetic (continuous for numeric position, discrete for categorical colour/fill); user-added scales override.
- GGPlot(VGroup) result with attributes .axes, .layers (dict keyed by layer name or index), .legend, .title and __getitem__ for 'axes' | 'layers' | 'legends' to preserve the old key access. Layout: panel at origin, legend per theme.legend_position, axis titles from labs()/scale names/mapped column names.
- build() must be pure: calling it twice on the same spec gives equivalent mobjects and never mutates the spec, the data, or user-supplied Mobjects.
- Remove the stray print in range inference.
acceptance_criteria: Structural tests: end-to-end plots for each ported geom; idempotent double build; GGManim(...).geom_point().build()['layers'][0] still works; auto-limit inference with mixed data/intercept layers; per-layer data override; unknown aesthetic column gives a clear error naming the column and layer.

title: Guides: legends for discrete scales with geom key glyphs
description:
Create guides.py.
- For each trained non-position scale (color, fill), build a Legend: title (scale name or mapped column), one row per level: key glyph + label. The glyph is produced by the geoms that use that aesthetic (Geom.draw_key); if several geoms map the same aesthetic, overlay their glyphs in one key (ggplot behaviour). Labels via theme.make_text.
- Merge legends whose aesthetics map the same column with identical levels (color + fill on one column -> one legend).
- Legend layout: vertical stack, optional SurroundingRectangle via theme; positioned by theme.legend_position (right/left/top/bottom/none) relative to the panel in the assembler.
- guides(color='none') component to suppress a legend.
acceptance_criteria: Structural tests: legend row count equals number of levels; glyph colour equals scale.map(level); colour+fill on the same column yields one legend; guides(color='none') removes it; legend labels use the Text engine by default.

title: CoordCartesian + Theme: manim Axes construction from trained scales
description:
Create coords.py and theme.py.
- Theme dataclass with fields for: text_engine ('text'|'tex', default 'text'), font_size for axis text/titles/legend, foreground colour (default derived from manim config.background_color: BLACK on light, WHITE on dark), axis line stroke width, tick length, whether to draw tick labels, legend position ('right' default), x_length/y_length of the panel (default fit manim frame with room for legend), text factory make_text(str|Mobject) -> Mobject that honours the engine and accepts ready-made Mobjects unchanged. theme_default(), theme_minimal(), theme_classic() as components.
- CoordCartesian: given trained x/y scales and theme, builds ONE manim Axes in transformed (linear) space with the scale's limits (incl. expansion) and breaks; replaces manim's numeric tick labels with the scale's label strings (so log10 axes show 10, 100, 1000 on a linear axis). Exposes transform(x, y) -> Nx3 points via a single vectorised axes.c2p call, panel_params (x/y range in transformed space), and axis title placement (x below, y rotated left) WITHOUT mutating caller-supplied Mobjects (copy before rotate).
acceptance_criteria: Structural tests: Axes x_range equals the scale's expanded limits; tick labels equal scale.get_labels(); transform of a (x,y) array equals axes.c2p per point; building twice from the same spec gives identically positioned labels; theme foreground follows config.background_color; text_engine='text' builds without LaTeX available.

title: Geoms: base class + port point, line, col, vline, hline, function, smooth
description:
Create geoms/base.py and one module per geom.
- Geom base: required_aes, default_aes (ggplot defaults: point size/alpha, line width, etc.), draw_panel(data, panel_params, coord, **params) -> VMobject, draw_key(data_row, theme) -> small VMobject used by legends. Constant (unmapped) aesthetics given as params (e.g. geom_point(color=RED)) override defaults; mapped aesthetics come from scaled data columns. Translation table from ggplot aesthetics to manim kwargs: color->stroke/color, fill->fill_color, alpha->opacity (fill_opacity/stroke_opacity), size->radius or stroke_width, linetype (solid only in Phase 1).
- geom_point: VGroup of Dot, positions from one vectorised coord.transform call; per-point colour/fill/alpha/size.
- geom_line: sort by x within group; one VMobject per group built with set_points_as_corners (do not use plot_line_graph); optional label= placed at each group's last point in the group's colour (fixes the last-group-only label bug).
- geom_col (identity bars; keep geom_bar as alias until stat_count lands in Phase 3): width in data units (default 0.9 of min x spacing), rectangle from min(max(0, ymin_limit)) to y, computed through coord.transform so it is correct on any transform; position in data space.
- geom_vline(xintercept)/geom_hline(yintercept): spans the panel's y/x range from panel_params; label= as before; constant colour honoured; these layers carry no data and must not participate in x/y scale training except through their intercepts.
- geom_function(fun): uses stat_function then draws like geom_line; label= at curve end.
- geom_smooth: stat_smooth then line for fit plus a filled ribbon (ymin/ymax) at low opacity when se=True.
acceptance_criteria: Structural tests per geom: point centres equal coord.transform(x,y); line vertex count equals group size and order is by x; col rectangles have the right width/height in scene units on linear and log10 x; vline/hline span the full panel; function and smooth produce one VMobject per group; constant colour overrides mapped default; mixing geom_function/vline with data layers in one plot builds with auto limits (regression for the KeyError).

title: Stats: base class, stat_identity, stat_smooth (lm), stat_function
description:
Create stats/base.py, stats/identity.py, stats/smooth.py, stats/function.py. Pure pandas/numpy; no manim imports.
- Stat base: required_aes, default_aes, compute_group(df, scales, **params) -> df; compute_panel splits by 'group' (derived from the discrete aesthetics present: color, fill, shape, linetype, group) and concatenates, preserving the grouping columns.
- stat_identity: passthrough.
- stat_smooth(method='lm', formula degree=1, n=80, se=True, level=0.95, fullrange=False): np.polyfit/lstsq, returns x, y, ymin, ymax, se columns. Use scipy.stats.t if importable else normal quantile. Drop scikit-learn.
- stat_function(fun, n=101, xlim=None): evaluates fun on a grid over the x scale range (vectorised; fall back to np.vectorize if fun is not array-safe).
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests: smooth on exact line recovers slope/intercept and zero-width band; grouped smooth fits per group; stat_function with scalar-only fun; stat output carries group columns through.

title: Scales core: continuous position scales, transforms, pretty breaks
description:
Create scales/base.py, scales/continuous.py, scales/breaks.py. Pure numpy; no manim imports.
- Scale base: aesthetics (tuple), name, train(values), map(values), get_limits(), get_breaks(), get_labels(), expand, limits (user override), oob policy (censor default), reset().
- Transform objects: identity, log10, sqrt, reverse with forward/inverse/breaks/format. Scale trains and computes breaks in transformed space (fixes the LogBase exponent-range bug: we never use manim LogBase).
- breaks.py: pretty(lo, hi, n=5) matching R's pretty() (1-2-5 nice numbers, snapping outward); log_breaks (powers of 10 + optional 2,5 minor); default label formatter (trim trailing zeros, scientific when |exp|>=5); expansion helper (mult=0.05 continuous).
- scale_x_continuous / scale_y_continuous(name, breaks, labels, limits, expand, trans); scale_x_log10 / scale_y_log10 as continuous with trans=log10; scale_*_reverse, scale_*_sqrt.
- xlim()/ylim() helpers create a scale with limits (censor semantics; 2-tuple only — the old 3-tuple [min,max,step] is replaced by breaks=).
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for pretty() against known R outputs (e.g. pretty(0,1)->0,0.2,...,1; pretty(0.003,0.07); pretty(-17,42)); log10 scale trained on [3, 2500] yields breaks 10,100,1000 and limits in log space with expansion; user limits censor out-of-range values to NaN; transform round-trips.

title: Discrete colour/fill scales and palette cleanup
description:
Create scales/discrete.py; rewrite palettes.py.
- palettes.py: palettes are plain lists of ManimColor (or hex strings) and/or callables n -> list[ManimColor]. Keep Tol BRIGHT and MUTED; add Tol VIBRANT and a default hue palette (ggplot2-like evenly spaced HCL/HSL hues). Delete HashableManimColor (it breaks len()/str() and only existed to defeat np.asarray).
- ScaleDiscrete base: train collects unique levels (respecting pandas Categorical order, else sorted); map levels -> palette values; raises a clear error if more levels than palette entries (or cycles when palette says so).
- scale_color_discrete / scale_fill_discrete (palette=...), scale_color_manual / scale_fill_manual(values=dict|list), scale_color_identity.
- Map output must be manim-ready: 'color' -> ManimColor for stroke/color, 'fill' -> fill_color.
- Declare which aesthetics are categorical by default (color, fill, shape, linetype) so build.py knows to use discrete scales when the mapped column is non-numeric; numeric color columns are out of scope (Phase 2 gradients) and should raise NotImplementedError with a helpful message.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests: levels order (categorical vs sorted), manual mapping by dict, too-many-levels error, map returns ManimColor instances, mapping is stable across layers that share the scale.

title: Plot spec: aes(), ggplot, Layer, .add() and generated chaining
description:
Create aes.py, plot.py, layer.py.
- aes(x=None, y=None, **kwargs): mapping of aesthetic -> column name or callable(df)->Series. Normalise ggplot aliases (colour->color, fill, size, alpha, shape, linetype, group).
- Layer dataclass: geom, stat, position, data (DataFrame|None), mapping (aes), params (dict), inherit_aes (bool), name (str|None).
- ggplot(data=None, mapping=None): immutable spec holding data, mapping, layers (list), scales (list), coord, facet, theme, labels. .add(*components, name=None) returns a NEW ggplot (shallow-copy spec; DataFrame shared by reference). Each component implements add_to(plot) -> plot so scales/themes/coords/labs/layers all go through one method.
- Component registry: every public component constructor (geom_*, stat_*, scale_*, coord_*, theme*, labs, xlab, ylab, xlim, ylim) is registered once; chaining methods on ggplot are generated from the registry (ggplot.geom_point(**kw) == self.add(geom_point(**kw))). No __add__.
- GGManim = alias for ggplot; keep .xlab/.ylab/.xlim/.ylim/.scale_x_log10/.scale_y_log10 working via registry.
- Fix: per-layer data must use 'is None' checks, never DataFrame truthiness.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests: .add returns a new object and leaves the original untouched; registry-generated methods exist for every registered component; layer-level data override works with a DataFrame; aes alias normalisation; name= stored on Layer.

title: Phase 1 — core refactor to the grammar of graphics
description: Replace the single-class GGManim prototype with ggplot2's architecture: immutable plot spec composed via .add() + generated chaining, Layer = geom+stat+position, Scale/Coord/Theme objects, and a 9-step build pipeline (see PLAN.md §2). Phase ends with functional parity for the existing geoms (point, line, function, vline, hline, smooth, bar→col), every defect in PLAN.md §1 fixed, tests green, and one example rendered. Prerequisite: Phase 0 hygiene (pyproject with manim/pandas/numpy, pytest, ruff) so tests can run.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads closed; pytest green; examples/basic.py renders with manim -ql; legacy GGManim.py removed; README updated to new API.

title: Theme elements: panel/plot backgrounds, axis text rotation, complete theme set
description:
Extend theme.py (frozen dataclass; keep the merge/overrides mechanism) and coords.py to cover the ggplot theme elements plots commonly need:
- panel_background (fill colour/opacity, default None), panel_border (theme_bw), plot_background, panel_grid_major / panel_grid_minor split (currently a single panel_grid), per-axis switches (axis_text_x/axis_text_y/axis_title_x/axis_title_y, axis_ticks_x/y, axis_line_x/y) so one axis can be blanked.
- axis_text_x_angle / axis_text_y_angle with hjust/vjust anchoring (rotated category labels on a discrete axis — pairs with S1), axis_text colour overrides, font family per element (text, axis_text, title...), plot_title_position ('panel'|'plot'), plot_margin.
- Complete themes with ggplot's looks: theme_gray (grey panel, white grid), theme_bw, theme_linedraw, theme_light, theme_dark, theme_minimal (exists), theme_classic (exists), theme_void; plus theme_manim() tuned for a black background (current default appearance).
- Tests: each complete theme builds; rotated tick labels are rotated by the angle and stay below the axis; blanked elements absent from the panel; merge of partial theme keeps other fields.
acceptance_criteria: All listed fields exist, are validated, and are documented in the Theme docstring; gallery renders theme_gray/bw/dark/void side by side.

title: Phase 2 gallery, README and regression tests
description: examples/gallery.py with one Scene per feature: categorical bar chart with rotated labels (S1+S9), colourbar heat-style scatter (S2), size legend (S3), shape+linetype legend (S4), merged legend + inside placement (S5), log axis with label_math and minor grid (S6), zoomed vs censored smooth side by side (S7), monthly time series (S8). CI renders all with -ql -s and uploads them. README: new 'Scales' and 'Guides' sections + the ggplot2 -> ggmanim cheat-sheet table listing supported scales/guides/themes. tests/test_regressions_phase2.py covering the seams closed in this phase (discrete x no longer raises; numeric colour no longer raises; mapped size/alpha scaled; shape/linetype drawn).
acceptance_criteria: CI green with the gallery artifact; README sections present; regression tests pass.

title: coord_cartesian zoom vs scale limits: semantics, oob, and geometric clipping
description:
coord_cartesian(xlim, ylim, expand) already zooms without censoring (coords.py). Make the ggplot semantics complete and tested, and clip marks to the panel.
- Verify/document: xlim()/scale limits censor BEFORE stats (a smooth fits only in-range data) while coord_cartesian zooms AFTER (fit uses all data, line extends to the panel edge). Add tests for both with geom_smooth.
- oob policies: 'censor' (drop + warning with count, like ggplot's 'Removed n rows'), 'squish' (clamp to limits), 'keep'; scales.continuous already defines them — ensure every geom honours NaN positions by dropping those rows (finite_rows) and that warnings are emitted once per layer.
- Clipping (clip='on' default on the coord): points outside the panel range are dropped; paths/polygons/ribbons/rects are clipped numerically (Liang-Barsky for segments; Sutherland-Hodgman for polygons) in geoms/base before mobject creation, so zoomed plots never draw outside the panel; clip='off' disables. vline/hline/abline naturally span the panel.
- coord_flip: swap x and y at panel build (axes, labels, geoms unchanged since they go through coord.transform) — cheap once transform is the single entry point; coord_fixed(ratio) sets panel aspect via theme.panel_size.
- Tests: zoomed smooth touches both panel edges; censored smooth does not; clipped polyline endpoints lie on the panel border; coord_flip puts the x column on the vertical axis; coord_fixed aspect.
acceptance_criteria: Semantics tests pass; a zoomed render shows no marks outside the panel; coord_flip and coord_fixed registered and exported.

title: Guide options: guide_legend / guide_colorbar, merging rules, legend placement & direction
description:
Extend guides.py beyond guides(aes='legend'|'none').
- guide_legend(title=None, nrow=None, ncol=None, byrow=False, reverse=False, override_aes=None, order=0, direction=None) and guide_colorbar(...) objects accepted by guides(color=...) and by a scale's guide= argument; GUIDE_TYPES grows accordingly; override_aes lets e.g. alpha=1 in keys.
- Merging: legends whose title AND levels (breaks+labels) match merge into one (colour+shape+size on the same variable -> one legend with composite keys), matching ggplot's merge rule; order= sorts legends.
- Placement: theme(legend_position=(x, y)) inside the panel in NPC coordinates [0,1]^2 plus legend_justification; legend_direction horizontal/vertical independent of position; legend_box='horizontal'|'vertical' for multiple legends; legend_key_size, legend_spacing, legend_title_align theme fields; legend background/border via theme.
- show_legend=False per layer already exists; add show_legend as a dict per aesthetic (ggplot allows show.legend = c(colour = FALSE)).
- Tests: merge of colour+shape on one column; no merge when titles differ; nrow/ncol layout counts; inside placement lands within the panel bbox; order= respected.
acceptance_criteria: Structural tests for every option; legend/colourbar coexist; README legend section.
notes: From 4a9.3: linetype legend keys compress patterns to KEY_SIZE/2 so dashed/longdash look alike — consider wider keys for linetype legends. From 4a9.5: legends and colourbar don't pass labels through labels.render_label, so label_math shows raw $...$ — route them through render_label(s, theme.text_engine).

title: Label formatters and break helpers (ggmanim.labels)
description:
New module ggmanim/labels.py (scales-package style, no manim imports) with callables usable as scale labels=/breaks=:
- label_number(accuracy=None, scale=1, prefix='', suffix='', big_mark=',', decimal_mark='.', trim=True), label_comma, label_percent(accuracy, scale=100), label_dollar/label_currency, label_scientific(digits), label_math(base=10) -> '10^k' strings rendered with superscripts (Unicode superscripts for the Text engine, LaTeX when theme.text_engine == 'tex'; the coord must pass the engine to the formatter or accept pre-made Mobjects), label_date (hands off to S8), label_wrap(width).
- breaks_pretty(n), breaks_extended(n) (Wilkinson's extended algorithm, port from the labeling R package; compare with pretty() in tests), breaks_width(width, offset), breaks_log(n, base), minor_breaks: scale minor_breaks= argument (default: one between majors; log: 2..9 multiples) exposed via get_minor_breaks(); coords.py draws minor grid lines when theme.panel_grid_minor is True (new field, default True, lighter stroke).
- scale_*_continuous(position='top'/'right') to put the axis on the other side; sec_axis is out of scope (note in docstring).
- Tests: formatter outputs for edge cases (0, negatives, 1e-7, 12345678.9, NaN), extended breaks for the classic Talbot et al. cases, minor breaks counts, position='top' moves tick labels above.
acceptance_criteria: All formatters/break helpers unit-tested; scale_x_log10(labels=label_math()) renders 10^k; minor grid visible in a render.

title: Remove legacy GGManim.py and dead code; finalise public API
description: After parity: delete ggmanim/GGManim.py, color_mapping, CATEGORICAL_AES, HashableManimColor and the funcy/sklearn imports; drop them from dependencies. __init__.py exports an explicit __all__ (ggplot, GGManim, aes, geom_*, stat_*, scale_*, coord_*, theme*, labs, xlab, ylab, xlim, ylim, guides, palettes). Delete ggmanim/gurobi.log. Run ruff + mypy clean.
acceptance_criteria: 'from ggmanim import *' exposes only __all__ names; grep finds no funcy/sklearn; ruff and mypy pass; package installs from a clean venv and the example renders.
notes: Also: remove stray print in legacy GGManim.py range inference (left from s11.8) — moot if file deleted. Legacy GGManim.py colour path broken since palette rewrite; legacy ggplot() no longer accepts palette=.

title: Regression tests for known defects + example gallery entry + README
description: Add tests/test_regressions.py with one test per row of the defect table in PLAN.md §1 (per-layer DataFrame; intercept-only layers with auto limits; nice breaks count 4-8 for assorted ranges; log10 axis labels; fill/shape/size/alpha mapped columns not leaking raw values into mobject kwargs; grouped line labels per group; double build idempotence; dark-background foreground). Add examples/basic.py (scatter + smooth + colour legend + log x) and render it with 'manim -ql -s' in CI as a smoke test. Rewrite README to the .add()/chaining API with three examples. Document that Tex is opt-in via theme(text_engine='tex').
acceptance_criteria: All regression tests pass; CI renders the example; README examples run as doctests or a script test.

title: Tolerance in _clip.clip_segments for near-parallel border segments
description: Liang-Barsky in geoms/_clip.clip_segments cuts segments lying ~1e-17 outside a panel edge at their midpoint; _marker_clip works around it by snapping. Move the tolerance into clip_segments so all geoms benefit. Follow-up from ggm-sxu.

title: guide_coloursteps for binned colour scales
description: Binned colour scales (scale_*_fermenter, ScaleBinnedColour) use a colourbar with nbin=100 approximating step edges; add guide_coloursteps/guide_colorsteps with exact step edges. Follow-up from ggm-buo.

title: Register geom_path constructor
description: GeomPath exists (geoms/line.py) but no public geom_path is registered/exported; needed e.g. for spirals. Also consider per-segment colour for geom_smooth and direct labels using segment colour. Follow-up from ggm-5wa.

title: scale_*_distiller / brewer palettes
description: ColorBrewer palettes (scale_color_brewer/distiller/fermenter). Deferred from 4a9.2.

title: Per-segment colour for geom_line with continuous colour
description: geom_line with a continuous colour mapping uses the first colour per group; ggplot colours each segment. Follow-up from 4a9.2.

title: Clip point markers at panel border
description: Points are dropped by centre only; a dot near the border can protrude by up to its radius. ggplot clips the drawn glyph. Consider clipping marker geometry or shrinking-at-border (follow-up from 4a9.6).

title: Date / datetime position scales
description:
scale_x_date / scale_y_date / scale_x_datetime (scales/date.py): a ScaleContinuousPosition whose transform maps datetime64 / date columns to float days (date) or seconds (datetime) since epoch; default scale chosen by dtype in build.setup_position_scales; breaks via date_breaks='1 month'|'2 weeks'|'1 year' (pandas offset aliases) or automatic pretty date breaks (choose unit from the span: years/months/weeks/days/hours); labels via date_labels strftime format or label_date(); limits accept dates/strings; expansion as continuous. Timezone handling: naive and UTC only in this phase.
- Tests: breaks for 3-day, 3-month and 5-year spans; strftime labels; limits as ISO strings; geom_line over a datetime x.
acceptance_criteria: A time series with a datetime64 column builds with sensible month/year ticks without the user adding a scale; unit tests for breaks and labels.
